## What

<!-- The change, present tense, a sentence or two. What the reader will find different. -->

## Why

<!-- The need it meets. If a measurement motivated it, give the number — not the investigation
     that found it. -->

## Approach

<!-- Only where a reviewer would otherwise propose the alternative: say briefly why this shape
     and not that one. Delete this section when the shape is uncontroversial. -->

## Verification

<!-- What was run, and what a reviewer can re-run (`cargo make check`, `cargo make test`, a
     package's --self-check). Name the test that fails if this regresses. -->

## Contract changes

<!-- A schema, theme-contract role, catalog or other published vocabulary this PR changes, and
     how: `added` / `changed` / `removed`. `none` when no contract moves. -->

<!-- ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
     Four rules (CONTRIBUTING.md → "PR guidelines").

     1. THE CODE CARRIES THE DETAIL. A rationale longer than a paragraph belongs in a comment
        next to the thing it explains, where it survives this PR being merged. Link to it.

     2. NO SESSION NARRATIVE. What was tried first, which probe was wrong, what an agent
        reported. The reviewer needs the change, not the path to it.

     3. THIS REPO IS PUBLIC. No specs, plans, gap inventories or temper resource ids — those
        live in the temper vault. Scope statements are welcome; an inventory of what remains
        weak is not.

     4. SAY WHAT IT DOESN'T DO, IN SCOPE TERMS. Reviewers infer coverage from silence; one line
        naming what this deliberately leaves alone is worth a paragraph of caveats.
     ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────── -->
